knowledge:
- key_parameters: Filter=Logical. In Linnorm and Linnorm.limma, filters out low count genes and genes with high technical noise ;; output=Character. In Linnorm.Norm, set to "XPM" if downstream tools convert data to CPM/TPM, or "Raw" if downstream tools require raw counts. In Linnorm.limma, set to "Both" to return both DEG results and the transformed matrix ;; BE_strength=Numeric. Controls normalization strength (default 0.5 to prevent overfitting; set to 1 to increase strength) ;; DataImputation=Logical. In Linnorm, set to TRUE to perform data imputation during transformation ;; RowSamples=Logical. Set to TRUE if columns represent genes and rows represent samples (improves speed) ;; input=Character. Set to "Linnorm" in compatible functions if the input dataset is already Linnorm-transformed to avoid redundant transformation ;; Group=Vector. In clustering functions, provides sample group/subpopulation annotations ;; num_center=Integer. In t-SNE/PCA clustering, specifies the number of clusters for k-means ;; num_PC=Integer. In t-SNE/PCA clustering, specifies the number of principal components to use ;; distribution=Character. In RnaXSim, specifies the simulation distribution ("NB", "Gamma", "Poisson", "LogNorm")
- alternatives: limma=Used internally by Linnorm.limma for differential expression analysis ;; Spike-in genes=Alternative to using Linnorm.SGenes for identifying stable genes in single-cell RNA-seq datasets
- when_to_use: Use when analyzing high-throughput count data (especially single-cell RNA-seq with high noise and zero inflation) to perform normalization, transformation, differential expression, clustering, or network analysis under parametric assumptions.
- pitfalls: Do NOT input log-transformed datasets, as Linnorm performs its own log transformation ;; Undefined values such as NA, NaN, and INF are not supported ;; Data imputation (Linnorm.DataImput) is not recommended unless it is explicitly shown to improve downstream results ;; Linnorm.Norm and Linnorm.SGenes must only be run on raw, pre-transformed data ;; Setting BE_strength too high can cause overfitting and artificially reduce biological differences between conditions

workflows.name: normalization_and_transformation
workflows.intent: Normalize, transform, and optionally impute raw count or expression data for downstream parametric analysis or export.
input: Islam2011 (matrix or data frame of raw counts or expression values where columns are samples and rows are genes)
workflows.stages: 1. Load the Linnorm library and dataset ;; 2. Perform normalizing transformation with or without low-count filtering ;; 3. Export transformed data to a tab-delimited file ;; 4. Perform normalization to XPM or Raw counts ;; 5. Optionally perform data imputation or select stable genes.
workflows.code:
library(Linnorm)

# Obtain data
data(Islam2011)

# Do not filter gene list:
Transformed <- Linnorm(Islam2011)

# Filter low count genes
result <- Linnorm(Islam2011, Filter=TRUE)
FTransformed <- result[["Linnorm"]]

# You can use this file with Excel.
# This file includes all genes.
write.table(Transformed, "Transformed.txt",
quote=FALSE, sep="\t", col.names=TRUE, row.names=TRUE)

# This file filtered low count genes.
write.table(FTransformed, "Transformed.txt",
quote=FALSE, sep="\t", col.names=TRUE, row.names=TRUE)

library(Linnorm)
Normalized <- Linnorm.Norm(Islam2011)

# You can use this file with Excel.
write.table(Normalized, "Normalized.txt",
quote=FALSE, sep="\t", col.names=TRUE, row.names=TRUE)

# Data Imputation
DataImputed <- Linnorm.DataImput(Transformed)

# Or, users can directly perform data imputation during transformation.
DataImputed <- Linnorm(Islam2011,DataImputation=TRUE)

# Obtain stable genes
StableGenes <- Linnorm.SGenes(Islam2011)

workflows.name: differential_expression_limma
workflows.intent: Perform differential expression analysis on count data using the integrated Linnorm-limma pipeline.
input: LIHC (matrix of raw counts or expression values)
IslamData (matrix of single-cell RNA-seq raw counts)
workflows.stages: 1. Define the experimental design matrix ;; 2. Run the Linnorm-limma pipeline to identify differentially expressed genes ;; 3. Extract and filter significant genes ;; 4. Generate a volcano plot.
workflows.code:
library(Linnorm)
data(LIHC)
datamatrix <- LIHC

# 5 samples for condition 1 and 5 samples for condition 2.
# You might need to edit this line
design <- c(rep(1,5),rep(2,5))
# These lines can be copied directly.
design <- model.matrix(~ 0+factor(design))
colnames(design) <- c("group1", "group2")
rownames(design) <- colnames(datamatrix)

library(Linnorm)
# The Linnorm-limma pipeline only consists of one line.
DEG_Results <- Linnorm.limma(datamatrix,design)

library(Linnorm)
# Just add output="Both" into the argument list
BothResults <- Linnorm.limma(datamatrix,design,output="Both")

# To separate results into two matrices:
DEG_Results <- BothResults$DEResults
TransformedMatrix <- BothResults$Linnorm

write.table(DEG_Results, "DEG_Results.txt", quote=FALSE, sep="\t",
col.names=TRUE,row.names=TRUE)

Genes10 <- DEG_Results[order(DEG_Results[,"adj.P.Val"]),][1:10,]

SignificantGenes <- DEG_Results[DEG_Results[,5] <= 0.05,1]

plot(x=DEG_Results[,1], y=DEG_Results[,5], col=ifelse(DEG_Results[,1] %in%
SignificantGenes, "red", "green"),log="y", ylim = 
rev(range(DEG_Results[,5])), main="Volcano Plot", 
xlab="log2 Fold Change", ylab="q values", cex = 0.5)

workflows.name: coexpression_network_analysis
workflows.intent: Identify gene co-expression networks, perform clustering, and visualize correlation profiles.
workflows.stages: 1. Run Linnorm.Cor to calculate gene correlation and identify clusters ;; 2. Plot the co-expression network using igraph ;; 3. Extract genes belonging to specific clusters ;; 4. Generate a correlation heatmap for top correlated genes.
workflows.code:
data(Islam2011)

# Obtain embryonic stem cell data
datamatrix <- Islam2011[,1:48]

results <- Linnorm.Cor(datamatrix, plotNetwork=FALSE,
# Edge color when correlation is positive
plot.Pos.cor.col="red",
# Edge color when correlation is negative
plot.Neg.cor.col="green")

Genes10 <- results$Results[order(results$Results[,5]),][1:10,]

library(igraph)
Thislayout <- layout_with_kk(results$igraph)
plot(results$igraph,
# Vertex size
vertex.size=2,
# Vertex color, based on clustering results
vertex.color=results$Cluster$Cluster,
# Vertex frame color
vertex.frame.color="transparent",
# Vertex label color (the gene names)
vertex.label.color="black",
# Vertex label size
vertex.label.cex=0.05,
# This is how much the edges should be curved.
edge.curved=0.1,
# Edge width
edge.width=0.05,
# Use the layout created previously
layout=Thislayout
)

TheCluster <- which(results$Cluster[,1] == "Mmp2")

# Index of the genes
ListOfGenes <- which(results$Cluster[,2] == TheCluster)

# Names of the genes
GeneNames <- results$Cluster[ListOfGenes,1]

top100 <- results$Results[order(results$Results[,4],decreasing=FALSE)[1:100],1]

Top100.Cor.Matrix <- results$Cor.Matrix[top100,top100]

library(RColorBrewer)
library(gplots)
heatmap.2(as.matrix(Top100.Cor.Matrix),
# Hierarchical clustering on both row and column
Rowv=TRUE, Colv=TRUE,
# Center white color at correlation 0
symbreaks=TRUE,
# Turn off level trace
trace="none",
# x and y axis labels
xlab = 'Genes', ylab = "Genes",
# Turn off density info
density.info='none',
# Control color
key.ylab=NA,
col=colorRampPalette(c("blue", "white", "yellow"))(n = 1000),
lmat=rbind(c(4, 3), c(2, 1)),
# Gene name font size
cexRow=0.3,
cexCol=0.3,
# Margins
margins = c(8, 8)
)

workflows.name: highly_variable_gene_analysis
workflows.intent: Identify highly variable genes/features from expression data.
workflows.stages: 1. Run Linnorm.HVar to detect highly variable genes ;; 2. Extract results and plot Mean vs SD highlighting significant genes.
workflows.code:
data(Islam2011)

# The first 48 columns are the embryonic stem cells.
results <- Linnorm.HVar(Islam2011[,1:48])

resultsdata <- results$Results
Genes10 <- resultsdata[order(resultsdata[,"q.value"]),][1:10,3:5]

print(results$plot$plot)

workflows.name: cell_subpopulation_clustering
workflows.intent: Perform cell subpopulation clustering using t-SNE, PCA, or Hierarchical Clustering.
workflows.stages: 1. Run t-SNE k-means clustering with or without known group annotations ;; 2. Run PCA k-means clustering with or without known group annotations ;; 3. Run Hierarchical Clustering and plot the dendrogram.
workflows.code:
library(Linnorm)
data(Islam2011)

tSNE.results <- Linnorm.tSNE(Islam2011[,1:92])

print(tSNE.results$plot$plot)

# The first 48 samples belong to mouse embryonic stem cells.
Groups <- rep("ES_Cells",48)
# The next 44 samples are mouse embryonic fibroblasts.
Groups <- c(Groups, rep("EF_Cells",44))

tSNE.results <- Linnorm.tSNE(Islam2011[,1:92],
 Group=Groups, num_center=2)

print(tSNE.results$plot$plot)

PCA.results <- Linnorm.PCA(Islam2011[,1:92])

print(PCA.results$plot$plot)

PCA.results <- Linnorm.PCA(Islam2011[,1:92],
Group=Groups, num_center=2, num_PC=3)

print(PCA.results$plot$plot)

Islam <- Islam2011[,1:92]

# 48 ESC, 44 EF, and 4 NegCtrl
Group <- c(rep("ESC",48),rep("EF",44))
colnames(Islam) <- paste(colnames(Islam),Group,sep="_")

# Note that there are 3 known clusters.
HClust.Results <- Linnorm.HClust(Islam,Group=Group,
num_Clust=2, fontsize=1.5, Color = c("Red","Blue"), RectColor="Green")

print(HClust.Results$plot$plot)

workflows.name: rnaxsim_expression_simulation
workflows.intent: Simulate RNA-seq expression data with known differentially expressed genes for method evaluation.
workflows.stages: 1. Run RnaXSim with default Negative Binomial distribution parameters ;; 2. Run RnaXSim with advanced parameters (e.g., Gamma distribution, custom replicates, and feature counts) ;; 3. Extract simulated expression matrices and true DE gene indices.
workflows.code:
library(Linnorm)
data(SEQC)
SampleA <- SEQC

# This will generate two sets of RNA-seq data with 5 replicates each. 
# It will have 20000 genes totally with 2000 genes being differentially 
# expressed. It has the Negative Binomial distribution.
SimulatedData <- RnaXSim(SampleA)

# Index of differentially expressed genes.
DE_Index <- SimulatedData[[2]]

# Expression Matrix
ExpMatrix <- SimulatedData[[1]]

# Sample Set 1
Sample1 <- ExpMatrix[,1:3]

# Sample Set 2
Sample2 <- ExpMatrix[,4:6]

library(Linnorm)
SimulatedData <- RnaXSim(SampleA,
distribution="Gamma", # Distribution in the simulated dataset.
# Put "NB" for Negative Binomial, "Gamma" for Gamma,
# "Poisson" for Poisson and "LogNorm" for Log Normal distribution.
NumRep=5, # Number of replicates in each sample set. 
# 5 will generate 10 samples in total.
NumDiff = 1000, # Number of differentially expressed genes.
NumFea = 5000 # Total number of genes in the dataset
)

# Index of differentially expressed genes.
DE_Index <- SimulatedData[[2]]

# Expression Matrix
ExpMatrix <- SimulatedData[[1]]

# Simulated Sample Set 1
Sample1 <- ExpMatrix[,1:3]

# Simulated Sample Set 2
Sample2 <- ExpMatrix[,4:6]
